name: Stephen Hawes
credit: No confirmed portrait sourced for this archive.
bio: Stephen Hawes was an English poet who served as a groom of the chamber to Henry VII, best known for his allegorical romance ‘The Pastime of Pleasure.’
His verse bridges medieval allegory and the new humanism of the early Tudor court, and he was among the last English poets to write in the tradition of Chaucer and Lydgate.

poems.title: The True Knight
poems.author: Stephen Hawes
poems.text:
For knighthood is not in the feats of warre,
      As for to fight in quarrel right or wrong,
    But in a cause which truth can not defarre:
      He ought himself for to make sure and strong,
      Justice to keep mixt with mercý among:
        And no quarrell a knight ought to take
        But for a truth, or for the common’s sake.

poems.title: An Epitaph
poems.author: Stephen Hawes
poems.text:
O mortal folk, you may behold and see
      How I lie here, sometime a mighty knight;
    The end of joy and all prosperitee
      Is death at last, thorough his course and might:
      After the day there cometh the dark night,
        For though the daye be never so long,
        At last the bells ringeth to evensong.
